unusual.text: The sub oscillators are true dividers: each counts its VCO’s cycles and plays its frequency divided by a whole number, 1 to 16. So a sub can only land on a note of the undertone series under its VCO, and it follows the VCO’s pitch and wave. The knob turns the wrong way for a pitch: fully right is unison, fully left the lowest.
One switch sets the wave of a VCO and both its subs. In the middle the VCO is a pulse whose width SUB 1’s sawtooth moves, which adds a pitched ripple at SUB 1’s note even with SUB 1’s level down.

There is no step length or gate pattern: four rhythm generators divide one tempo by whole numbers and each steps either or both sequencers. Two or more on one sequencer make a polyrhythm that repeats when they meet on a downbeat.
A sequencer can move a sub’s divisor instead of its VCO’s pitch: the steps then climb and fall the undertone series under a VCO that stays put, so a sequence can never go out of key with its chord.

QUANTIZE snaps both VCOs and both sequencers at once, and offers just intonation as well as equal temperament: 12-JI and 8-JI tune intervals to whole-number ratios, so chords stop beating. The 8-step scales are C major, rooted on C.
SEQ OCT is shared: one button sets how far a step reaches on both sequencers, ±1, ±2 or ±5 octaves. The sequencers cannot push a VCO above about 10 kHz, so the widest range wants FREQ fully left.

The envelopes have only attack and decay, and are played by the sequencer steps rather than by keys: EG off lets the steps change pitch without playing a note, and EG held opens both envelopes for a drone. An envelope cannot restart during its own attack, so a long attack lets only some steps through.
VCF EG AMT works both ways: right of centre the envelope opens the filter, left of centre it closes it.
Keys (MIDI notes on the hardware) play as an offset from C4 on both VCOs, so with FREQ fully left they sound as written; with PLAY lit they transpose the running sequence.

limits.intro: The sound path and the sequencing are modelled: both VCOs with their three waves, the four subs as true dividers, the six-level mixer, the ladder filter, both attack–decay envelopes and the VCA; the clock, the four rhythm generators, both sequencers with ASSIGN, SEQ OCT and QUANTIZE (12-ET, 8-ET, 12-JI and 8-JI), PLAY, RESET, NEXT, TRIGGER and EG off, on and held; and every patch point but MIDI IN, with the hardware’s normals.

items.title: What is not modelled
items.text: Holding QUANTIZE or SEQ OCT to decouple the SEQ outputs; Fine Tune; Rhythm Generator Logic, which is set over MIDI on the hardware and is always OR here; holding RESET to hold step 1 (a gate at the RESET input does it) and holding TRIGGER as a gate with EG off; MIDI CCs, note priority, the MIDI channel and transport settings. MIDI clock is the app’s own: Play on the bar clocks the sequencers at four clocks a beat, as a MIDI clock would, and TEMPO sets the bar’s tempo.

items.title: The app’s readings of the manual
items.text: The manual prints no knob numbering, so knobs here run 0 to 10 and the STEP knobs and VCF EG AMT −5 to +5. Its ranges are used where it gives them (FREQ C4 to C8, CUTOFF 20 Hz to 20 kHz, ATTACK 1 ms to 10 s, DECAY 5 ms to 10 s, TEMPO 20 to 3,000 BPM); the tapers between them, VCF EG AMT’s depth at full (eight octaves here), how far a volt moves a divisor (1.5 here), and the 12-JI ratios are this app’s. The 8-JI ratios are the manual’s just C major example, not confirmed.

items.title: What the sources leave open
items.text: How MIDI notes gate the envelopes, and whether they reach both VCOs, are not described: here a key plays on both VCOs, gates both envelopes while the sequencers are stopped, and while they run never holds the envelopes open, firing them only with EG off. XOR with three or more rhythms on one sequencer is not stated. The pitch bend range is not published.
